headline: Sony Music says the number of AI deepfake tracks it has asked streaming services to remove has doubled in six months.
score_reason: Company figures, not independently checked; shows the scale of the problem.
importance_line: Fans may be tricked by fake songs in a famous artist's voice, and artists lose money and control, though Sony's figures are its own and platforms have not responded in the article.
summary: MusicRadar reports that Sony Music says it has asked streaming platforms to remove 260,000 AI deepfake tracks imitating its artists in the year to September, against 135,000 in the year to March. Sony calls enforcement "an uphill struggle" and wants platforms to stop the same content from reappearing; the figures are Sony's own.
